# Idle-workbench and stale pipeline-run reports in the web console

## Description

Delivers per-project administrator reports in the RHOAI web console that
surface idle and stale resources so administrators can reclaim capacity with
confidence: an idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved
resources) sourced from the notebook controller's existing activity tracking,
and a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age,
with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. Either
report can be exported as CSV. The reports are read-only views; automated
reclamation and cost/chargeback calculations are out of scope for this
strategy.

## Scope

- Add a per-project idle-workbench report to the console: for each workbench
  in a project, show last activity, owner, and reserved resources, sourced
  from the notebook controller's activity tracking (the data already exists;
  no notebook controller changes are in scope).
- Add a per-project stale pipeline-run report to the console: list completed
  pipeline runs older than a configurable age threshold together with their
  retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata (no
  pipeline component changes are in scope).
- Make the stale-run age threshold configurable.
- Provide CSV export of either report.
- The reports are read-only: no reclamation or deletion actions are offered
  (automated reclamation and cost/chargeback calculations are out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing activity, when an
  administrator opens the idle-workbench report, then every workbench in the
  project is listed with its last activity, owner, and reserved resources —
  measured by the report matching the notebook controller's activity tracking
  for the same workbenches.
- Given a project with completed pipeline runs of differing ages, when an
  administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report, then completed runs older
  than the configured age threshold are listed with their retained artifacts —
  measured by the report matching Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata for the same
  runs.
- Given a different stale-run age threshold is configured, then the stale
  pipeline-run report filters runs according to the new threshold.
- Given either report is displayed, when the administrator exports it, then a
  CSV file is produced containing the report's rows and columns as displayed.
- The reports present information only and offer no reclamation or deletion
  actions.
- The console change builds successfully and the existing console build
  pipeline stays green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): the web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last
  activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's
  activity tracking — covered by the idle-workbench report scope and ACs
  above.
- HLR-2 (P1): the web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed
  runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from
  Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata — covered by the stale pipeline-run report
  scope and ACs above.
- HLR-3 (P2): administrators can export either report as CSV — covered by the
  CSV export scope and AC above.

## Assumptions

- The strategy asserts the underlying data already exists (the notebook
  controller tracks last-activity timestamps; Kubeflow Pipelines retains run
  completion metadata) and declares no open questions. The exact interfaces
  through which the console reads this data are left to the implementing team;
  the "measured by" clauses above validate the assumption. If the activity
  data proves unreadable by the console through existing interfaces, follow-up
  work in the owning components (Notebooks, owned by the Workbenches team)
  would be raised separately.
